post.caption:
The Big Bang produced hydrogen, helium and a trace of lithium. That is the whole list. Every heavier atom was fused inside stars, step by step over billions of years, and a star cannot build past iron because beyond that fusion costs energy rather than releasing it. So the heaviest elements came from the deaths: supernovae and neutron star collisions. The iron in your blood and the calcium in your bones were made by something that had to die first.
